req.title: Redirect preserves relative or absolute style
req.statement: The system shall emit relative URLs on /redirect/<n> and absolute URLs on /absolute-redirect/<n>.
triggers: redirect preserves relative or absolute style

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect/<n> emits relative URLs and /absolute-redirect/<n> emits absolute URLs. The source code shows redirect_n_times uses request.args 'absolute' param to toggle behavior, and _redirect helper is called with 'relative'/'absolute' style. Tests must verify: (1) positive - relative redirect on /redirect/<n>, (2) positive - absolute redirect on /absolute-redirect/<n>, (3) boundary - n=1 (minimum valid), (4) boundary - n=0 triggers assertion error (NEG), (5) negative - invalid n type returns 404, (6) DT - absolute=true query param on /redirect/<n> produces absolute URL. Mutation resilience requires exact status code assertions, exact Location header prefix checks (relative vs absolute), and boundary ±1 on n.

tests.name: test_relative_redirect_location_is_relative_url
expected: Location header starts with '/' (relative, not http://)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_relative_redirect_location_is_relative_url():
    r = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location.startswith('/'), f"Expected relative URL starting with '/', got: {location}"
    assert not location.startswith('http://'), f"Expected relative URL, got absolute: {location}"
    assert not location.startswith('https://'), f"Expected relative URL, got absolute: {location}"

test_relative_redirect_location_is_relative_url()

tests.name: test_redirect_n0_is_invalid_negative
preconditions: n=0 (below minimum, assert n>0 in source)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: n=0 violates assert n>0 in redirect_n_times; must not produce a redirect
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n0_is_invalid_negative():
    r = client.get('/redirect/0', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code != 302, f"n=0 should not produce a 302 redirect, got {r.status_code}"
    assert r.status_code in (400, 404, 500), f"Expected error status for n=0, got {r.status_code}"

tests.name: test_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_relative
actions: GET /redirect/2 follow_redirects=False to get first Location
GET that Location follow_redirects=False to get second Location
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: state transition through redirect chain preserves relative style at each hop
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_relative():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers['Location']
    assert loc1.startswith('/'), f"First hop must be relative, got: {loc1}"
    assert not loc1.startswith('http'), f"First hop must not be absolute, got: {loc1}"
    r2 = client.get(loc1, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers['Location']
    assert loc2.startswith('/'), f"Second hop must be relative, got: {loc2}"
    assert not loc2.startswith('http'), f"Second hop must not be absolute, got: {loc2}"

test_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_relative()

tests.name: test_absolute_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_absolute
expected: Second Location is also absolute URL
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: state transition through absolute-redirect chain preserves absolute style at each hop
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_absolute_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_absolute():
    r1 = client.get('/absolute-redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers['Location']
    assert loc1.startswith('http://') or loc1.startswith('https://'), f"First hop must be absolute, got: {loc1}"
    path = loc1.split('localhost', 1)[-1] if 'localhost' in loc1 else '/absolute-redirect/1'
    r2 = client.get(path, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers['Location']
    assert loc2.startswith('http://') or loc2.startswith('https://'), f"Second hop must be absolute, got: {loc2}"

test_absolute_redirect_chain_n2_second_hop_absolute()

tests.name: test_redirect_non_integer_n_returns_404
expected: HTTP 404 (Flask route type mismatch for int:n) — NOT 302
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: non-integer n must not produce a redirect; Flask int converter rejects it
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_non_integer_n_returns_404():
    r = client.get('/redirect/abc', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 404, f"Expected 404 for non-integer n, got {r.status_code}"
    assert r.status_code != 302, "Non-integer n must not produce a redirect"
